subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What happens to chest volume and pressure during inhalation?
options: Volume increases, pressure decreases so air flows in
questions.explain: The chest volume increases, lowering the pressure inside so air is drawn into the lungs.

questions.q: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Which gas is needed for aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen to break down glucose fully.

questions.q: Which products show that aerobic respiration has taken place?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration releases carbon dioxide and water as products.

questions.q: Which structure carries air from the throat towards the lungs?
questions.explain: The trachea (windpipe) carries air down towards the bronchi and lungs.

questions.q: Where does gas exchange take place in the lungs?
questions.explain: The alveoli are tiny air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged.

questions.q: Plant and yeast cells respiring anaerobically produce ethanol; this process is also called...
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration in yeast and plants is known as fermentation.

questions.q: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast?
questions.explain: In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: On which surface of a leaf are stomata usually most numerous?
questions.explain: Stomata are usually concentrated on the lower surface, reducing water loss.

questions.q: What controls the opening and closing of stomata?
questions.explain: Guard cells change shape to open or close the stomata.

questions.q: The fermentation of sugars by yeast is used in which industries?
questions.explain: Yeast fermentation produces carbon dioxide for bread and ethanol for alcoholic drinks.

questions.q: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy than aerobic respiration per glucose molecule?
options: Glucose is only partially broken down
questions.explain: Without oxygen glucose is incompletely broken down, so less energy is released.
